Putting Together What @elonmusk is Saying/Doing

AI Demand
1. Just yesterday, Elon said "Agentic demand is growing faster than I’ve ever seen anything grow" (1).
2. His actions match "I've been personally spending a lot of time in Memphis, often 4 days a week" (2). $SPCX's biggest goal in terms of revenue next year will be bringing 10GW of compute online.

Financing Availability
1. Now Elon is saying "debt markets have almost entirely shut off access to money for any company that doesn’t have substantial revenue independent of AI data centers". 

Conclusion
Elon basically sees AI as the biggest opportunity in the coming years and is doing whatever he can to bring compute online. Now he is saying no one else besides him and hyperscalers will be financed to do it.

So I ask you: Is this how America works? The biggest business opportunity of our time only available to the richest man and the richest companies? Is this Elon's patriotic vision for America?

quoted_tweet.author: Elon Musk
quoted_tweet.text:
Pretty much. 

As of the past few weeks, debt markets have almost entirely shut off access to money for any company that doesn’t have substantial revenue independent of AI data centers. 

SpaceX closed $40B of debt for GPUs, but we’re investment grade and have Starlink & launch revenue.

That means the 200+ neoclouds are going to see guppy-level death and consolidation. Some will make it through, but not many.

text:
I don’t understand the problem here. Elon is stating two simple facts:

1) AI demand is exploding.
2) Lenders are becoming more risk-averse.

What does any of this have to do with patriotism or America? This is capitalism. Nobody is entitled to a loan.

It’s like blaming banks for not lending to risky individuals. Of course they don’t want their money wasted. Banks don’t lend based on how exciting an industry is. They lend based on risk and the borrower’s ability to repay.

SPCX has substantial revenue outside AI compute. Most neoclouds don’t. That’s a fact, and from a lender’s perspective it’s a massive difference.

If lenders decide they’re overexposed to AI infrastructure and want to cut their risk, why exactly should they be blamed? And why should companies with stronger financials be blamed for still having access to capital?

Elon isn’t saying only rich companies deserve to succeed. He’s telling what’s happening behind the curtain with lenders, and what that means for *most* neoclouds. 
Turning that into moral outrage about America and “the rich get richer while the little guy gets screwed” is very cheap imo

quoted_tweet.author: Xiaoyin Qu
quoted_tweet.text:
My take: SaaS is dead. Software is charity now, make money elsewhere. 

No one can make $$ selling the same features for years anymore. 

Instead: 
- Use good software to collect user data and sell data. 
- Use good software to deliver outcome and sell outcome. 
- Arbitrage tokens under the guise of selling software - buy bulk, sell retail. 
- Use good software internally to drive your own margin higher for your services/products
- Build RSI agent in a domain that has the fastest learning loop so it has the most, latest expertise: e.g. a marketing agent that knows the latest tricks to get viral in X coz it's doing it for others every day and learn and evolve. 
- Give away all your features for free, it's futile anyways. Open source them. Make money elsewhere.
